correctness.rationale: Every zero falls into a controlled inner or outer rescaled region by a quantitative triangle-inequality dichotomy. Limiting maps have exactly k and n+k isolated simple roots, respectively, with nonzero signed Jacobians, so compactness and the real-analytic implicit-function theorem prove an exhaustive count and uniform first-order expansions without numerical enumeration. Phase equality with gcd(n,k)=1 proves exact nearest/farthest elementary bounds; the finite angular root-of-minus-one arithmetic and positive coefficient gap establish the two odd-degree farthest conjugate roots and the quantified positive parity defect. The exact exponent of the big-O remainder follows from R epsilon_o squared. CHECK.py passed 39 finite tests as diagnostics only.

value.rationale: The 2020 paper poses the location problem for this exact family, and 2022 literature supplies coarse annular/sector inclusions. Determining both asymptotic root constellations with explicit first angular and radial displacements gives a natural complete localization theorem for all coprime exponent pairs. The sharp odd-n outer-radius defect quantifies the nonattainment of the standard sharp even-n radius bound and rigidly identifies the farthest two roots, which is not recoverable from an unrefined annulus. The claim is structural and motivated rather than a finite table or cosmetic improvement.
